results.summary_before: This project implements the measurement-update step of a basic Kalman filter as a fixed-function hardware accelerator in a single Tiny Tapeout tile. It performs matrix operations and includes a register file for storing state and covariance values. The design is intended for digital signal processing applications and is notable for its fixed-point arithmetic and FSM-based control. It is verified with a cocotb testbench.
results.summary: This project implements a standalone bit-serial CORDIC sine generator in a single Tiny Tapeout tile. It uses a bit-serial CORDIC engine with fixed-point output and a DDS phase accumulator to generate a sine wave on uo[7] and a phase-locked square wave on uo[6]. The design is verified with exhaustive angle tests, FFT analysis, and formal control-path proofs, not with a cocotb testbench. It outputs an analog sine via an RC low-pass filter or the Tiny Tapeout Audio Pmod, along with a heartbeat LED and a level bar.

results.summary: This project implements a ternary bit-serial MNIST handwritten digit classifier in a 4x2 tile Tiny Tapeout design. It uses a ternary-weight neural network with a distribution-free conformal early exit that stops classification when the answer is decided. The design supports loading config bytes and pixel data over an 8-bit bus, with control pins on the bidirectional lines. It is implemented in SystemVerilog and targets embedded AI inference applications.
